data.narrative:
Aeva Technologies is a public-stage semiconductor company founded by Soroush Salehian and Mina Rezk, currently valued at $1.09B after raising $660M+. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of 3 public peers in Chips & Semiconductors (Cerebras, Credo Semiconductor, Ouster) and 8 private-stage frontier semiconductor firms.

The peer-median method is the primary applicable triangulation approach. The median valuation across the 3 same-sector, same-stage public comparables stands at $35.8B, with a range spanning $2.3B (Ouster floor) to $39.2B (Cerebras ceiling). A public-comp anchoring approach using price-to-sales multiples (median 18.9x across ALAB, NVDA, AMD) cannot be applied, as Aeva's revenue is not disclosed—a common limitation in private company valuation.

The triangulated range supports $30.4B to $41.2B, centered at $35.8B, derived from the single applicable method. The wide peer dispersion ($2.3B to $39.2B) reflects material uncertainty around stage maturity, technology differentiation, and path to profitability within the semiconductor subsector. Critical unknowns include Aeva's current revenue run-rate and gross margins relative to peers; without these metrics, multiple-based refinement remains infeasible. The valuation is primarily anchored to public comparables trading at substantial premiums, suggesting market pricing reflects early-stage frontier-tech risk rather than near-term profitability.
